part_title: Regulated Data Sharing and Encryption Design Decisions

scenes.title: Regulated cross-account encrypted data
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains regulated cross-account encrypted data by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The producer account on the left sends sensitive objects over HTTPS to a central data account. The data account owns an S3 bucket using SSE-KMS and its customer managed KMS key. The analyst account on the right needs authorized access to both the S3 object and its encryption key, including relevant cross-account policies. Below, a separate security account provides reviewed policy administration and auditing without automatically owning the data key. The numbered decision boxes summarize protected storage, both permissions and audit evidence.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Separate producer, data owner, security reviewer and analytics roles while retaining key ownership.

The producer account on the left sends sensitive objects over HTTPS to a central data account. The data account owns an S3 bucket using SSE-KMS and its customer managed KMS key. The analyst account on the right needs authorized access to both the S3 object and its encryption key, including relevant cross-account policies. The numbered decision boxes summarize protected storage, both permissions and audit evidence. Separate producer, data owner, security reviewer and analytics roles while retaining key ownership. When deciding what architecture to implement, first identify the caller, resource owner and trust boundary. Check how AWS policy authorization, service configuration and operational recovery interact instead of assuming a single setting makes everything secure. The diagram is a decision aid: follow its arrows from the original actor to the final action, and verify each dependency in the running environment.

scenes.title: Four encryption architecture decisions
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains four encryption architecture decisions by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The central application has four decision branches. At rest, use service encryption, data keys and suitable KMS policies. In transit, establish TLS policies, trusted certificate chains and endpoint validation. For key custody, choose standard KMS, CloudHSM or external key stores only when the requirements justify their management obligations. Finally, assess post-quantum readiness: inventory cryptography and consider ML-KEM shared secrets and ML-DSA signatures where supported. The closing strip asks architects to verify access, ownership and recovery at every boundary.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
No single encryption feature substitutes for transport, access control, key custody and recovery planning.
